correctness.rationale: For each nonreal deficiency parameter \(z=\pm i\), the primary source reduces the quantum-graph deficiency problem to the weighted discrete Laplacian. On each terminal tooth the exact equation gives \(f_{\mathrm{tooth}}=f_{\mathrm{spine}}/(1-z a^2)\). Substitution leaves a two-component spine recurrence. One initial spine value determines every solution, so the deficiency dimension is at most one. Finite total length implies summability of both spine lengths and the reduced coefficients q_k; a discrete Grönwall/infinite-product estimate bounds the unique nonzero formal solution. Since the total vertex measure is twice the finite edge length, the bounded solution is in \(\ell^2(V;m)\), giving dimension at least one. This is done for both signs. The packaged exact-arithmetic checker verifies the local algebra on asymmetric rational examples but is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2017 source explicitly states deficiency one for its finite-total-length comb as an expectation rather than a theorem. The 2022 graph-end theory gives only a general lower bound for a one-ended finite-volume graph unless an additional Sobolev-domain condition is established; its equality theorem for family-preserving metric graphs uses metric symmetry absent from arbitrary unequal tooth lengths. The new recurrence supplies the missing upper bound for the asymmetric comb. No covering published statement was found in the targeted literature searches.

value.rationale: The primary source itself singles out the missing deficiency count immediately after its finite-length self-adjointness analysis. The exact value \((1,1)\) determines the extension-theoretic boundary dimension of the model and separates this comb from later one-ended finite-volume constructions with arbitrarily large deficiency. Allowing unequal tooth lengths removes a genuine symmetry assumption rather than adding a cosmetic parameter.
